input.quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
input.rationale: Section 7.2 imposes the MFN on us, not the Vendor: we must disclose and match for Vendor "any more favourable commercial offer" we receive, with no product limitation, no time limit and no comparison carve-outs. That is the walk-away position (an open-ended obligation to extend better third-party terms to Vendor) and fails the fallback, which would require a defined product, a 12-month cap and reasonable-comparison exceptions. It also conflicts directly with Section 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges that we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment. We therefore delete Section 7.2 to reach the preferred position; no Vendor-granted MFN exists in the document that would be affected.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We deleted the requirement that we disclose and match third-party offers for Vendor: our playbook does not accept most-favoured-nation obligations running against the customer, and this one is open-ended. It also contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have given no most-favoured-customer commitment.
proposal.summary: Delete Customer-side MFN/match obligation in Section 7.2
